title: CHAPTER THREE. On the offices of Jesus Christ; prophetic, priestly, and kingly
english: CHAPTER THREE. On the offices of Jesus Christ.

The office of Jesus Christ is threefold: prophetic, priestly, and kingly. Since all offices are instituted for a certain end, and therefore have the character of means to obtaining that end, we will not badly measure Christs offices by the notion of His name. He is called JESUS CHRIST by words that belong to this person by excellence, of which the former indicates the ratio of the offices that serve this end.

The word Jesus signifies savior and physician. To save is to keep safe from evils — either by preventing them from coming on, or by removing them if they have prevailed — and consequently by conferring contrary goods. The worst of evils are sin and its wages, eternal death. The best of goods are righteousness and eternal life. He is therefore Savior in the most excellent mode, because He frees from sin and eternal death and confers righteousness and life (Matthew 1:21).

The word Christ denotes the anointed, from the anointing that under the Old Testament was done with oil, which because by natural efficacy it made bodies both fragrant and agile was fit to signify two supernatural things: the consecration of a person to some divine munus, and the collation of the gifts necessary for it.

title: II–VIII. Prophetic office: imposition, sanctification, instruction, promise of help
english: II. The PROPHECY of Christ is considered both in its imposition and in its execution. III. This prophecy of Christ is not only that He confirmed the old law and the evangelical promise made to the fathers of the Old Testament, but that He more fully disclosed the new gospel.

IV. In the imposition are contemplated sanctification, instruction, and the promise of help. V. SANCTIFICATION is that by which Christ was separately destined and consecrated by the Father to the prophetic munus. VI. INSTRUCTION is that by which the gifts necessary for prophecy were conferred on Him. VIII. The PROMISE of help is that by which the Father promises His aid to the Son for discharging this munus.
Christs prophecy is necessary to eternal salvation, because without the knowledge of God and of Christ salvation does not come about.

title: XIV–XVI. Priestly office: preparation and function of the high priest
english: XIV. In the priesthood of Christ are considered preparation and function. XV. Preparation is that of the priests vocation and consecration, by which the Son of God is destined and anointed to the priestly office.

XVI. The function of the munus consists both in the oblation of the sacrifice for sins and in intercession with the Father. Our Christ is high priest (Hebrews 2:11; 4:14; 5:6; 10:21), the Lamb of God (John 1:36), our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7), and advocate (1 John 2:1). Through sufferings He was consecrated to the priestly and kingly office.

title: XIX. Kingly munus: titles and pertaining acts
english: It is called kingly because it properly belongs to a king to govern, judge, and defend his people. Christ is king (Zechariah 9:9; Revelation 17:14), prince of the kings of the earth (Revelation 1:5), prince of peace (Isaiah 9:6), leader (Matthew 2:6), ruler (Micah 5:2), and judge (Acts 10:42; 2 Timothy 4:8).

XIX. To the kingly office pertain (1) the calling and gathering of the church; (2) its governance by Word and Spirit; (3) defense against enemies; (4) the final judgment. The means by which the kingly office is administered in the church are chiefly the Word and the efficacy of the Holy Spirit, which ought by no means to be separated from each other.

title: Cap.3 close: Word and Spirit inseparable; Cap.4 next on the states of Christ
english: For the Holy Spirit Himself ordinarily uses the Word or the senses of the Word in its external preaching (2 Corinthians 3:6). And the Word alone, apart from the Holy Spirits illumination and inspiration, does not suffice for the humans edification, as was shown above in Book I chapter 8. And Christ does not separate these two except by the fault of those who despise the Word and resist the Holy Spirit (Acts 7:51; Luke 7:30).

Events opposite to the predicted outcome are the casting off of Christs right, the imputation of sin, the denial or removal of the Holy Spirit, and handing over into Satans power, into a reprobate mind, hardness of heart, and besides temporary evils eternal death.
CHAPTER FOUR follows, On the states of Christ.
